title: Reject zero-occurrence recurring schedules before persistence
evidence_required: FT-002-AC-009 / REQ-004: RED: with valid ISO dates and a valid weekday selection that has no occurrence in the inclusive range, the current implementation returns schedule_created and persists a zero-Lesson schedule; GREEN: the corrected implementation returns HTTP 400 with the existing { error: 'invalid_schedule' } envelope before any Schedule or Lesson write, leaves schedule/Lesson state-before/state-after identical, and preserves the valid-occurrence success path; artifact: .tasks/TASK-032-T2-FT-002-W16/ and .protocols/TASK-032-T2-FT-002-W16/.
purpose: Ensure Center & Scheduling never persists an empty recurring schedule when a valid date range and weekday selection produce zero actual occurrences.
success_outcome: An authorized zero-occurrence schedule command is rejected atomically through the existing invalid_schedule 400 contract before schedule or lesson mutation, while valid-occurrence scheduling and the protected browser form continue unchanged.
anti_goals: Do not modify the completed TASK-031 card, protocol, evidence, localStorage implementation, or browser-draft test.
Do not change the completed TASK-026 card, protocol, evidence, authorization ownership, or protected UI behavior.
Do not introduce a new public error envelope, schema migration, dependency, server draft store, or persistence model.
Do not alter valid-occurrence recurrence, lesson identity, add/transfer/cancel behavior, or unrelated validation semantics.

stop_conditions: Stop if the rejection cannot use the existing Admin 400 invalid_schedule envelope without a new public error contract.
Stop if any schedule or lesson row is written before the zero-occurrence decision or if rollback/state equality cannot be demonstrated.
Stop if implementation requires changing AC-008 localStorage behavior, the protected UI, authorization scope, schema, dependencies, or valid-occurrence behavior.

constraints: Center & Scheduling remains the sole owner of Schedule and Lesson persistence; validate the occurrence list before the insert transaction mutates state.
Expose only the existing Admin HTTP 400 invalid_schedule error envelope for this expected input failure; any internal sentinel is private to the owner/adapter.
Keep TASK-031 browser draft retention/cleanup and valid-occurrence schedule creation as unchanged prerequisites and regression checks.
Use the existing inclusive ISO-date recurrence basis and weekday domain 0..6; no recurrence exceptions or schema changes are introduced.
invariants: A zero-occurrence request creates neither a schedules row nor a lessons row and leaves all relevant state unchanged.
Every failed zero-occurrence attempt returns HTTP 400 with error invalid_schedule through the existing Admin action path.
A request with at least one matching date still creates the planned lessons expected by the existing recurrence tests.
Authorization and center/class scope are checked before the command and remain unchanged.
verification_targets: FT-002-AC-009 server boundary RED/GREEN: in fresh isolated database state, authorized Admin submits canonical valid dates and a valid weekday with no match; capture current zero-lesson schedule_created and row counts, then prove 400 invalid_schedule plus exact schedule/Lesson state-before/state-after equality after the fix.

Protected browser/action probe: submit the same zero-occurrence form through the existing Admin action, observe the exact failure envelope and absence of schedule_created, and confirm the matching TASK-031 draft remains available without changing the localStorage implementation or claiming AC-008 ownership.
Regression: retain existing valid recurring schedule, authorization, lesson identity, and exception tests; add only the minimal server/action no-occurrence assertions needed for AC-009.

Source and transaction review: prove Center & Scheduling computes occurrence dates and rejects the empty result before schedule/lesson inserts, with route mapping limited to the existing invalid_schedule contract; run npm run check, npm run build, and npm run test.
